title: Stream from List
problem: Create a Stream from a List and print each element.
why: Canonical collection source for Stream pipelines.
trap: Reusing a Stream after a terminal operation throws IllegalStateException.
senior: Prefer forEach for pure side effects; use collect when you need a result.

title: Stream from Set then sort
problem: Stream unique departments and sort for stable output.
why: Set already unique; sorted makes output deterministic.
trap: Assuming HashSet encounter order is stable.
senior: Document ordering contracts when APIs return Sets.

title: Stream Map entries
problem: Print map entries as key=value lines.
why: Map itself is not a Stream source; stream the entrySet.
senior: Use LinkedHashMap when insertion order must be preserved.

title: Primitive IntStream sum
problem: Sum an int[] without boxing.
why: Primitive streams avoid Integer boxing overhead.
trap: Using Stream<Integer> on large arrays wastes CPU and GC.
senior: Prefer IntStream/LongStream/DoubleStream for numeric hot paths.

title: Stream.generate with limit
problem: Generate 5 random doubles safely from an infinite source.
why: Infinite sources must be bounded before a terminal op.
senior: Prefer RandomGenerator (Java 17+) when you need reproducible tests.

title: Files.lines try-with-resources
problem: Count non-blank lines in a CSV using Files.lines and ensure the file is closed.
why: Files.lines returns a Stream that holds an open file channel.
senior: Always close Files.lines / BufferedReader.lines in production code.

title: Optional.stream flatten
problem: Flatten a List of Optional<String> into present values only.
why: Optional.stream() yields 0 or 1 element — ideal for flatMap.
trap: filter(Optional::isPresent).map(Optional::get) is noisier and easier to misuse.

title: Filter even numbers
problem: Keep even integers from a list.
why: filter keeps elements matching a Predicate.
trap: Mutating the source list while streaming.
senior: Keep predicates pure and side-effect free.

title: Predicate and / or / negate
problem: Keep salaries that are either junior band (<50k) or executive band (>=200k) using composed Predicates.
why: Predicate composition avoids nested boolean soup and is reusable.
trap: Negating a complex predicate without parentheses clarity.
senior: Name predicates; compose with and/or/negate for interview clarity.

title: Filter non-blank strings
problem: Remove null and blank strings after trim.
why: Null-safe filtering before mapping prevents NPEs.
senior: filter(Objects::nonNull) early; prefer isBlank over isEmpty for whitespace.

title: Filter employees by department
problem: Return Engineering employees only.
why: Domain filtering is the most common Stream use case.
senior: Prefer constants or enums for department codes.

title: takeWhile / dropWhile sorted prefix
problem: From a sorted transaction amount list, take while amounts stay under 1000, then dropWhile under 100.
solution:
List<Integer> under1k = amounts.stream().takeWhile(a -> a < 1000).toList();
List<Integer> from100 = amounts.stream().dropWhile(a -> a < 100).toList();
why: takeWhile/dropWhile require sorted (or prefix-meaningful) encounter order.
trap: Using takeWhile on unsorted data and expecting a global filter.
senior: Interview: contrast takeWhile (prefix) vs filter (all matches).

title: Map to uppercase
problem: Transform strings to uppercase.
trap: Confusing map with flatMap for nested lists.
senior: Prefer method references when the mapping is a single method call.

title: mapToInt for salaries
problem: Compute average salary as double without boxing in the average step.
why: mapToInt yields IntStream with numeric terminals.
senior: Use mapToInt/Long/Double for aggregates on primitives.

title: Extract employee names
problem: Map Employee records to name strings.
why: Projection is the core map pattern in domain models.
senior: Records + method refs keep projections readable.

title: map vs peek side effects
problem: Demonstrate that peek should not replace map for transformations.
why: peek is for debugging; map returns the new value.
trap: Relying on peek for business logic (may be elided).
senior: Staff answer: peek is not guaranteed to run for short-circuit ops.

title: mapMulti for conditional emit
problem: Use mapMulti to emit square only for even ints (Java 16).
why: mapMulti is an imperative flatMap alternative with less allocation.
trap: Overusing mapMulti when filter+map is clearer.
senior: Prefer filter+map unless you need 0..N emits with shared state in the lambda.

title: Flatten list of lists
problem: Flatten List<List<String>> into one list.
why: flatMap maps each element to a stream and concatenates.
trap: Using map instead of flatMap leaves Stream<Stream<T>>.
senior: flatMap = map + flatten; interviewers watch for the nested Stream type.

title: Orders to line items
problem: From orders, collect all SKUs across line items.
why: One-to-many domain navigation is the textbook flatMap case.
trap: Null items list without Optional/emptyStream guard.
senior: Model empty collections as empty lists, not null.

title: Split sentences to words
problem: FlatMap sentences into lowercase words.
why: String.split returns array; Arrays.stream bridges to Stream.
trap: Pattern.compile per element instead of reusing Pattern.

title: flatMapToInt code points
problem: Sum Unicode code points of all strings.
why: codePoints handles supplementary characters correctly vs chars().
senior: Prefer codePoints for internationalized text processing.

title: Nested Optional flatMap
problem: Chain Optional lookups with flatMap then bridge into a Stream.
why: Optional.stream turns absent into empty contribution.
trap: Calling get() without isPresent in a map.
senior: Never Optional.get in Streams; use stream()/orElse.

title: Distinct strings
problem: Remove duplicate tags preserving encounter order.
why: distinct uses equals/hashCode; encounter order for sequential.
trap: distinct on objects without proper equals/hashCode.
senior: For custom uniqueness, use toMap/collectingAndThen or a LinkedHashSet collector.

title: Distinct-by-key warning (parallel)
problem: Explain why a stateful distinct-by-key with a shared HashSet breaks under parallel().
why: Shared mutable Set in filter is a race under parallel and a hidden side effect.
trap: filter(seen.add) in parallelStream — lost updates / ConcurrentModification.
senior: Staff: distinct-by-key needs ConcurrentHashMap or toMap merge; never a plain HashSet in parallel.

title: Distinct after map
problem: Map orders to customerId then distinct.
why: distinct after projection is cheaper than distinct on heavy objects.
trap: distinct before map when only the projected key matters.
senior: Project early; distinct on the key you care about.

title: Distinct primitives
problem: Unique ints via IntStream.
why: Primitive distinct uses a specialized set.
trap: Boxing then distinct on Stream<Integer> for large arrays.
senior: Stay on IntStream for numeric uniqueness.

title: Natural sort strings
problem: Sort names alphabetically.
trap: sorted() on streams of non-Comparable types.
senior: Provide Comparator when natural order is wrong for the domain.

title: Sort employees by salary desc
problem: Sort employees by salary descending, then name ascending.
why: thenComparing breaks ties stably for reporting.
trap: comparing salary as Integer nulls without nullsLast.
senior: Always define a total order for production sorts.

title: Sort BigDecimal amounts
problem: Sort payment amounts ascending with BigDecimal.
why: BigDecimal.compareTo ignores scale; equals does not — know the difference.
trap: Using equals for money uniqueness vs compareTo for sort.
senior: FinTech: never sort money as double; use BigDecimal.

title: reverseOrder
problem: Sort integers descending.
why: reverseOrder is the concise descending Comparator.

title: Top 3 with limit
problem: Take first 3 elements after sorting descending.
why: limit short-circuits after N elements when ordered.
senior: For top-N, sort then limit — or use a heap for large n.

title: Pagination skip/limit
problem: Page size 10, page index 2 (0-based) of transaction ids.
trap: Deep offsets on huge streams are expensive.
senior: Prefer keyset pagination in production APIs.

title: skip first header
problem: Skip CSV header line then parse.
why: skip drops the first N encounter-order elements.
trap: skip on unordered parallel sources is nondeterministic.
senior: Keep header handling sequential when order matters.

title: limit on infinite iterate
problem: Materialize first 100 primes-like candidates from iterate (illustrative bound).
why: limit is mandatory on infinite sources.
senior: Library APIs should require a bound for infinite factories.

title: anyMatch / allMatch / noneMatch
problem: Check if any employee is in ENG, all have salary > 0, none are contractors.
trap: allMatch on empty stream is true (vacuous truth).

title: findFirst vs findAny
problem: Contrast findFirst and findAny on parallel streams of payment ids.
solution:
Optional<String> first = ids.stream().filter(id -> id.startsWith("P")).findFirst();
Optional<String> any = ids.parallelStream().filter(id -> id.startsWith("P")).findAny();
why: findFirst respects encounter order; findAny may return any match (faster parallel).
trap: Assuming findAny is deterministic under parallel.
senior: Use findFirst when order matters; findAny when any witness is enough.

title: findFirst present name
problem: Find first name starting with A.
senior: Prefer orElseThrow in domain code when absence is a bug.

title: Short-circuit vs full scan
problem: Show anyMatch can stop early vs count() always scans.
solution:
boolean ok = huge.stream().anyMatch(x -> x == 42);
long n = huge.stream().filter(x -> x == 42).count(); // full scan
why: Choose the terminal that matches the question.
trap: Using collect just to check existence.
senior: Interview: pick anyMatch for existence, findFirst for the value.

title: max / min with Comparator
problem: Find employee with max salary.
trap: max on empty stream — handle Optional.
senior: For ties, chain thenComparing to define a winner.

title: Sum with reduce
problem: Sum integers with reduce.
why: Identity must be identity for the operator.

title: Reduce with combiner (parallel)
problem: Implement parallel-safe String joining of account ids with reduce identity/accumulator/combiner.
why: Combiner merges partial results from parallel splits; must be associative.
trap: Omitting combiner on parallel reduce of non-associative ops.
senior: Staff: joining Collector is clearer; know combiner for whiteboard reduce.

title: Reduce BigDecimal totals
problem: Sum payment amounts with BigDecimal reduce.
senior: ZERO is the correct identity for add.

title: Optional reduce without identity
problem: Find longest string via reduce without identity.
solution:
Optional<String> longest = words.stream()
  .reduce((a, b) -> a.length() >= b.length() ? a : b);
trap: Assuming reduce always returns a value.

title: Mutable reduction anti-pattern
problem: Show why reduce into a shared mutable List is wrong vs collect.
why: collect is designed for mutable reduction; reduce for immutable folds.
trap: Identity ArrayList shared across threads if mis-specified.
senior: Architect: use collect for mutable accumulators; reduce for pure folds.

title: toList / toSet / toCollection
problem: Collect names to List, Set, and LinkedList.
why: Choose the collection semantics you need.
senior: Java 16 toList() is unmodifiable; use toCollection for mutable.

title: summarizingInt
problem: Get count, sum, min, max, average of salaries in one pass.
trap: Multiple separate sum/min/max passes on huge lists.

title: averaging / summing
problem: Average and sum of order totals.
solution:
double avg = orders.stream().collect(Collectors.averagingDouble(o -> o.total().doubleValue()));
BigDecimal sum = orders.stream().map(Order::total).reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
why: averagingDouble is convenient but lossy for money — prefer BigDecimal sum.
senior: FinTech interviews fail people who average money as double.

title: counting collector
problem: Count elements with Collectors.counting.
trap: Using counting when stream.count() is enough.
senior: Prefer stream.count() unless nesting in groupingBy.

title: collectingAndThen wrap unmodifiable
problem: Collect to a mutable list then wrap as unmodifiable via collectingAndThen.
why: collectingAndThen finishes a downstream result with a finisher function.
trap: Returning the same mutable list from the finisher.

title: groupingBy department
problem: Group employees by department.
trap: Assuming map iteration order is sorted.
senior: Use groupingBy(classifier, TreeMap::new, downstream) for sorted keys.

title: groupingBy with counting
problem: Count employees per department.
why: Downstream collectors specialize the value type.
trap: Expecting Integer instead of Long from counting.

title: groupingBy summing salaries
problem: Sum salary per department.
why: Downstream numeric collectors avoid manual reduce.
trap: summingInt overflow for huge payrolls — use summingLong.
senior: Prefer Long for money-like ints at scale.

title: Nested groupingBy
problem: Group by department then by title.
trap: Deep nesting without a view/DTO becomes unreadable.
senior: Staff: two-level grouping is common; three+ levels need named types.

title: groupingBy averagingDouble
problem: Average order value per customer.
trap: Money as double in financial ledgers.
senior: For money, group then reduce BigDecimal separately.

title: groupingBy mapping names
problem: Map department → list of employee names.
why: mapping adapts element type before downstream collect.
trap: Forgetting mapping and ending with List<Employee> when names needed.
senior: mapping + joining is a frequent interview combo.

title: groupingBy collectingAndThen max
problem: Per department, the highest-paid employee (Optional unwrapped).
solution:
Map<String, Employee> top = employees.stream()
  .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Employee::department,
      Collectors.collectingAndThen(
          Collectors.maxBy(Comparator.comparingInt(Employee::salary)),
          Optional::orElseThrow)));
why: Finish Optional downstream into a concrete value.
trap: orElseThrow when a group could theoretically be empty (it won't after grouping).

title: groupingBy to Set
problem: Unique job titles per department.
why: toSet downstream deduplicates within each group.
senior: Choose Set vs List based on reporting needs.

title: groupingByConcurrent
problem: Parallel group transactions by currency.
why: Concurrent grouping for parallel pipelines; key order not defined.
trap: Using groupingBy (non-concurrent) with parallelStream and shared mutable state.
senior: groupingByConcurrent returns ConcurrentMap; don't rely on ordering.

title: groupingBy filtering downstream
problem: Per department, only employees with salary >= 100000.
why: filtering downstream keeps empty groups for departments with no matches.
trap: Pre-filter before grouping drops empty department keys.
senior: Interview nuance: filter before vs Collectors.filtering.

title: groupingBy teeing aggregates
problem: Per merchant, compute count and total amount together (teeing inside groups via custom approach).
solution:
record Stats(long count, BigDecimal total) {}
Map<String, Stats> byMerchant = payments.stream()
  .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Payment::merchantId,
      Collectors.teeing(
          Collectors.counting(),
          Collectors.mapping(Payment::amount, Collectors.reducing(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add)),
          Stats::new)));
why: teeing runs two downstream collectors and merges results.
trap: Writing two separate grouping passes on large ledgers.
senior: Java 12+ teeing is a staff-level collector answer.

title: groupingBy order status
problem: Count orders by status (NEW, PAID, SHIPPED).
senior: Prefer enums for finite domain statuses.

title: groupingBy year-month
problem: Group trades by YearMonth of trade date.
senior: Use java.time classifiers, never legacy Date strings.

title: groupingBy with TreeMap and summing
problem: Department payroll report with departments sorted alphabetically.
why: Supplier map type controls key ordering.
trap: HashMap when UI expects sorted keys.
senior: Pass map factory as second groupingBy arg.

title: groupingBy flatMapping skills
problem: Union of skills per department.
why: flatMapping flattens nested collections inside a group.
senior: Java 9 flatMapping is the clean nested-collection answer.

title: partitioningBy predicate
problem: Partition integers into even/odd.
why: Always returns both true and false keys.
trap: Expecting missing key when one side is empty — key still present with empty list.

title: partitioningBy employees high earner
problem: Partition employees by salary >= 150000.

title: partitioningBy with downstream counting
problem: Count paid vs unpaid invoices.
trap: Ignoring that both keys always exist.

title: partitioningBy prime check
problem: Partition 1..20 into primes vs non-primes.
solution:
Map<Boolean, List<Integer>> parts = IntStream.rangeClosed(1, 20).boxed()
  .collect(Collectors.partitioningBy(n -> n > 1 && IntStream.rangeClosed(2, (int)Math.sqrt(n)).noneMatch(d -> n % d == 0)));
why: Illustrates partitioning with a non-trivial predicate.
trap: Calling isPrime with trial division in a hot path without caching.

title: joining with delimiter
problem: Join names with comma and space.
why: joining is the idiomatic Collector for String concatenation.
trap: reduce with + for many strings (quadratic risk).
senior: Prefer Collectors.joining over manual StringBuilder in Streams.

title: toMap with merge function
problem: Build Map sku→qty merging duplicate SKUs by summing quantities.
solution:
Map<String, Integer> qty = items.stream()
  .collect(Collectors.toMap(LineItem::sku, LineItem::qty, Integer::sum));
why: Merge function resolves duplicate keys; without it duplicates throw.
trap: toMap without merge on duplicate keys → IllegalStateException.
senior: Always provide merge when keys may collide.

title: toMap last-win LinkedHashMap
problem: Index employees by id keeping insertion order; last duplicate wins.
solution:
Map<String, Employee> byId = employees.stream()
  .collect(Collectors.toMap(Employee::id, Function.identity(), (a, b) -> b, LinkedHashMap::new));
why: Four-arg toMap controls map type and collision policy.
trap: First-win vs last-win ambiguity in ETL.
senior: Document merge policy in data ingestion code.

title: joining with prefix suffix
problem: Render SQL IN clause list.
trap: SQL injection if ids aren't sanitized — Streams don't make SQL safe.
senior: Use parameters/bind variables; joining is only for display or trusted ids.

title: toMap with BigDecimal merge
problem: Aggregate ledger entries accountId → balance delta.
solution:
Map<String, BigDecimal> balances = entries.stream()
  .collect(Collectors.toMap(Entry::accountId, Entry::amount, BigDecimal::add));
why: Merge with BigDecimal::add for monetary aggregation.

title: Top N salaries
problem: Return top 3 salaries descending.
trap: For huge n, sort-all is wasteful vs heap of size k.
senior: Mention PriorityQueue for O(n log k) follow-up.

title: Nth highest distinct vs non-distinct
problem: Find 2nd highest distinct salary vs 2nd highest allowing duplicates.
why: Interviewers test whether you distinct before ranking.
trap: Forgetting distinct when the problem says unique salaries.
senior: Clarify distinct vs multiset ranking before coding.

title: Nth order by total
problem: Find the 3rd largest order by BigDecimal total.
senior: State n clearly; off-by-one is the common bug.

title: Top N per group
problem: Top 2 earners per department.
solution:
Map<String, List<Employee>> top2 = employees.stream()
  .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Employee::department,
      Collectors.collectingAndThen(Collectors.toList(), list -> list.stream()
          .sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(Employee::salary).reversed())
          .limit(2)
          .toList())));
why: Per-group top-N needs finisher sort or a custom accumulator.
senior: Staff follow-up: bounded PriorityQueue per group.

title: First N words
problem: Take first 5 words from a list.
why: limit without sort = first encounter order.
trap: Calling this top-N when order isn't ranked.
senior: Name the method carefully: prefix vs top.

title: Frequency map with groupingBy
problem: Build frequency map of words.
senior: groupingBy+counting is the default interview answer.

title: Find duplicates only
problem: Return elements that appear more than once.
trap: Using distinct thinking it returns duplicates.
senior: distinct removes dups; it does not list them.

title: First non-repeated character
problem: Find the first character in a string that appears exactly once.
solution:
Optional<Character> first = "swiss".chars()
  .mapToObj(c -> (char) c)
  .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Function.identity(), LinkedHashMap::new, Collectors.counting()))
  .entrySet().stream()
  .filter(e -> e.getValue() == 1)
  .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
  .findFirst();
why: LinkedHashMap preserves first-seen order for 'first' semantics.
trap: HashMap loses encounter order for first-non-repeated.

title: Mode of a list
problem: Find the most frequent integer (mode).
trap: Undefined behavior on ties — specify policy.

title: Duplicate emails in employees
problem: List emails that appear more than once.

title: Count characters
problem: Count occurrences of a character in a string via chars().
why: chars() is IntStream of UTF-16 code units.
trap: chars() vs codePoints() for supplementary chars.

title: Anagram check with Streams
problem: Check if two strings are anagrams (ignore case, ignore spaces).
why: Anagrams share the same sorted character multiset.

title: Reverse words in sentence
problem: Reverse word order using Streams.

title: Join with joining
problem: CSV-join tokens.

title: Longest word
problem: Find longest word in a sentence.

problem: Keep palindromic tokens ignoring case.

title: First non-repeated char (string category)
problem: Return first non-repeated character or empty.

title: Remove duplicate chars preserve order
problem: Distinct characters in encounter order.

title: Count vowels
problem: Count vowels in a word.
senior: Use Locale.ROOT for ASCII-oriented interview problems.

title: Group words by length
problem: Map length → list of words.

title: Pattern.splitAsStream

title: StartsWith filter

title: Longest common prefix via Streams (pairwise reduce)
problem: Find LCP of a list of strings using reduce.

title: Sort by length then alpha
problem: Sort words by length ascending, then alphabetically.
trap: Only sorting by length leaving unstable ties.

title: Array to Stream sum
problem: Sum int array.
trap: Stream.of(intArray) boxes to Stream<int[]> one element.

title: Two lists zip via IntStream
problem: Zip names and scores into 'name=score' strings.
trap: Assuming lists same size without check.

title: Partition list by predicate to two lists
problem: Split numbers into evens and odds lists via partitioningBy.

title: Sliding window sums

problem: Materialize String stream to array.

title: Stream map values
problem: Collect values greater than 10.

title: Invert map (value → list of keys)
problem: Invert Map<String,String> grouping keys by value.

problem: Return keys sorted by value descending.

title: Merge two maps with Streams
problem: Merge two Map<String,Integer> summing values for common keys.
solution:
Map<String, Integer> merged = Stream.concat(m1.entrySet().stream(), m2.entrySet().stream())
  .collect(Collectors.toMap(Map.Entry::getKey, Map.Entry::getValue, Integer::sum));

title: Department skill matrix
